Subject: POC traffic profile & evaluation gates — Quantum Health

Hi Alicia — great call today, thanks for walking through the use case. Quick recap and next asks so we can lock the POC scope: 

Recap
- Goal: Validate real-time clinical note summarization and query assistant integrated into provider portal. Target is reliable latency and cost at expected daily load.
- Key success criteria we discussed: consistent latency under SLA, acceptable output quality on our seeded eval set, and no data leakage.

Traffic & workload asks (need by EOD Wed so we can size the trial):
- Steady-state RPS (average): ?
- Peak RPS and burst characteristics (e.g., short spikes, minutes long): ?
- Typical prompt length (tokens) and typical response length (tokens) — if you have distributions, send percentiles (p50/p90/p99).
- Concurrency: how many simultaneous end-users/requests during peak?
- Any nightly batch/ingest jobs that will hit the service?

POC outline (high level) — we will formalize once we get the numbers:
1) Week 0: account onboarding + SOC2 & network checklist
2) Week 1: traffic ingestion + baseline run (unoptimized model)
3) Week 2: perf tuning (batching, quantization profiles) + eval on seeded prompts
4) Week 3: resiliency tests and burst simulation
5) Week 4: customer-facing validation + success signoff

Attachments: proof-of-concept-plan-v1.pdf (draft) — contains preliminary eval questions and a template for sample traffic CSV.

Can you confirm owners on your side and share the sample traffic CSV + any compliance constraints (data residency, PII flow)? Once we get the profile I’ll convert this into a formal SOW and timeline.

Thanks,
Dev

--

Thanks Dev — happy to confirm details. Below are the numbers from our telemetry and a couple notes on traffic patterns. Apologies for the delay, ran the numbers with infra.

Traffic profile (production-like simulator values)
- Avg steady RPS: 3 requests/sec (our background usage from scheduling and API traffic to the assistant)
- Typical peak: 25 RPS sustained for short windows (1–3 minutes) during morning rounds; biggest bursts observed: 60 RPS for spikes of ~30 seconds during shift handoffs.
- Prompt token lengths: median 48 tokens, p90 220 tokens (most use-cases are short queries but some clinical paste-ins are long)
- Response token lengths: median 180 tokens, p90 800 tokens, rare long reports up to ~4000 tokens when exporting notes
- Concurrency: ~8 concurrent active users during peak (our front-end multiplexes a few requests per user)
- Nightly batch: yes — a scheduled digest job generates ~4k docs overnight but it can be redirected off the POC if needed.

Compliance & constraints
- Data is US-only (no EU residency needed), PHI will be PII-protected; we need to keep an audit trail and not persist any raw PHI in third-party logs. SOC2 documentation would be required for procurement.

Owners
- Product lead: Alicia Ramos (me) — overall signoff
- Engineering lead: Tom Nguyen <tom@quantumhealth.ai> (cc not included here for brevity) — responsible for sample traffic and ingestion scripts
- Procurement: procurement@quantumhealth.ai — will handle contract & PO once we confirm pricing and SOW

I attached sample_traffic_profile.csv (CSV) — it's a small extract (timestamps, request_type, prompt_tokens, response_tokens). Let us know if the format works for you.

Alicia

Alicia — thanks, that's super helpful. Based on the traffic you shared I sketched a POC evaluation plan and performance targets below. Please review and flag anything you want adjusted.

POC evaluation gates (proposal)
- Performance: p95 end-to-end latency < 700ms for responses up to 256 tokens under peak simulated load of 25 RPS; for long-report flows (responses >1k tokens) we target steady-state throughput validation rather than strict p95 latency.
- Reliability: request error rate < 1% during 2-hour sustained run at peak RPS; successful fallback to a smaller model variant when capacity constrained.
- Quality: automated eval on seeded set — F1/ROUGE-like metrics target >= 0.8 vs. your human-labeled summaries; manual spot checks for clinical accuracy (Alicia/Tom to designate 8 clinicians for blind review).
- Cost: demonstration run with cost estimate provided; target is to identify optimizations to reduce unit cost by at least 20% versus baseline.
- Observability: request tracing and token-level cost breakdown available for each request; retention of request-level audit info for the POC (read-only access for Quantum Health).

Proposed timeline (4 weeks, can stretch to 6 if you prefer more validation):
- Week 0 (this week): SOC2 checklist, infra access, get sample CSV (received)
- Week 1: ingest sample traffic into staging, baseline run at 3–5 RPS + smoke tests
- Week 2: scale tests to 25 RPS with burst simulations up to 60 RPS, perf tuning (batching + KV cache settings)
- Week 3: quality evaluation on seeded set, clinician spot-checks, tweak model routing and quantization
- Week 4: final validation + signoff, handoff to procurement for PO

Owners on Redwood side
- Dev Patel (me) — technical lead / perf tuning / ops
- Monica Patel — eval set & quality leads; coordinates clinician reviews
- Jonas Weber — backend engineer for ingestion and synthetic traffic driver

Small asks for you to unblock the plan
1) Confirm Tom is comfortable sharing a 24-hour sample dataset (CSV or S3 link).
2) Confirm the list of clinicians (8 names) for manual review and a contract point-of-contact for the pilot (procurement).
3) Let me know if you need a 6-week timeline rather than 4.

I'll update the attached POC plan and generate a SOW doc once we agree.

Thanks,
Dev
